subject: Processing locations, subprocessors, and cross-border handling
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finserve.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on processing locations & subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FinServe is generally positive about Redwood but our compliance team has a focused set of questions before legal will move forward. Can you confirm the following at a high level so I can pass to our security lead: 

1) Where is customer data processed and stored by default (regions)? Are there options to restrict processing to specific regions?
2) Which subprocessors do you engage for hosted inference, telemetry/analytics, and logging? Do you have a recent list we can review?
3) How are cross-border transfers handled (e.g., EU->US or APAC->US)? Any SCCs or transfer mechanisms in place?
4) What are your default retention periods for request logs, KV caches, and training telemetry? Can data be purged on request?

If you can provide a one-page summary + any attachments (matrix or list), that would be ideal. Our security contact is security@finserve.com — feel free to loop them in.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — they want this in the week.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Product Security
FinServe Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finserve.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations & subprocessors

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short summary and attached our residency matrix and the latest subprocessor list. High-level answers below; Neha (security) is looped to add any technical detail.

1) Processing locations: Our hosted API runs in multiple cloud regions (US: us-west-2, us-east-1; EU: eu-west-1; APAC: ap-northeast-1). By default requests route to the nearest available region for latency, but customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private can pin processing to a region or VPC. The matrix shows default behavior and available region-restriction options.

2) Subprocessors: Primary subprocessors include the underlying cloud provider for compute/storage (AWS), a telemetry provider for aggregated usage metrics (TelemetryCo), and a logging provider (LogStream). The attached PDF is our canonical subprocessor list as of 2025-07 and includes contact/legal reps for each. For Dedicated/private deployments we can reduce/remove some subprocessors per contract.

3) Cross-border transfers: For hosted deployments, cross-border transfers occur when request routing or model hosting crosses region boundaries (e.g., EU->US) — we support region pinning for EU-residency requirements. For contractual controls we offer EU SCCs and a DPAs addendum; our privacy/legal team can provide the executed SCCs or equivalents. For transfers to the US we can also offer contractual commitments around data minimization and encryption.

4) Retention & deletion: Default request logs and lightweight telemetry are retained for 90 days for observability and billing. Persistent artifacts like KV caches are ephemeral and maintained only for the duration of the session (configurable TTL, default 24 hours). We offer customer-initiated purge on hosted accounts via support ticket and programmatic deletion for private deployments as part of the admin API. The attached matrix shows retention windows per artifact type and available retention controls.

Attachments: data-residency-matrix-v1.xlsx, subprocessor-list-2025-07.pdf

Neha — anything to add on encryption/SCCs?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-14T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations & subprocessors

Looping in a couple of technical clarifications so we have a single precise answer for the customer. Feel free to paste the bullets below into a formal response.

- Encryption: All data in transit uses TLS1.2+; data at rest in hosted regions is encrypted using AES-256. Keys are managed by the cloud provider by default; for enterprise contracts we offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for both Dedicated and Private.

- SCCs & transfer mechanisms: We have a standard DPA that includes the EU SCCs (post-2018 framework). For customers requiring additional assurances we can provide executed SCCs or reference our binding contract terms; legal can sign bespoke addenda for regulated verticals.

- Subprocessor detail: The attached subprocessor PDF lists the role (compute/storage/monitoring/logging), country of operation, and whether data stored is persistent. For hosted inference the most common cross-border movement is between cloud regions for model cache warm-up; persistent customer data stays in the region unless model routing policy explicitly spans regions.

- Deletion workflow: For hosted customers we process deletion requests in two phases: (1) soft-delete (remove from indexes/caches within 48 hours), (2) back-end purge (wipe backups/logs per retention schedule; can take up to 30 days for full backup cycle). For Dedicated/Private we can contract shorter SLAs for purges.

If you want, I can prepare an annotated PDF for FinServe's security team with excerpts from our DPA and the relevant SCC text.

-Neha
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-07-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations & subprocessors

Hi Daniel / FinServe security team — following up with a concise Q&A that summarizes the points Neha made and the attachments. I also included links to our SOC 2 report and DPA templates in the HubSpot/Drive links attached below. Short answers for your review: 

Q: Can you restrict processing to EU only?
A: Yes — we support region pinning for Hosted (via support request for enterprise accounts), and region restriction is standard for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q: Who are your subprocessors?
A: See attached list. Primary categories: cloud compute/storage (AWS), telemetry (TelemetryCo), model telemetry & metrics (Redwood Analytics — internal), and logging (LogStream). We update the list quarterly and notify customers of material changes.

Q: What transfer safeguards do you have?
A: EU SCCs via DPA, contractual commitments for cross-border transfers, AES-256 at rest, TLS for transit, and option for customer-managed keys.

Q: How do deletion requests work?
A: Submit a request to support@redwood.ai or via the admin console; we do a soft-delete within 48 hours and a full purge within the backup retention cycle (typically up to 30 days). Dedicated/Private customers can negotiate faster purges.

Next steps: if you want the annotated DPA + SCC excerpts I mentioned, Neha can assemble and we can route completed SCCs through legal. Rishi will coordinate legal signatures and timelines if FinServe wants executed SCCs.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call with FinServe security next week if that helps.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
